problem: If ${z}_{1}=5-2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=3\text{i}$, then ${z}_{1}$ divided by ${z}_{2}$ equals
worked_solution:
First, we set up the fraction:

$$
\frac{5-2\text{i}}{3\text{i}}
$$

The denominator is the imaginary number $3\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+3\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-3\text{i},$ or simply $-3\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}} & =\frac{5-2\text{i}}{3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{5-2\text{i}}{3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-3\text{i}}{-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-15\text{i}+6{\text{i}}^{2}}{-9{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-15\text{i}+6(-1)}{-9(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-6-15\text{i}}{9}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-6-15\text{i}}{9}=-\frac{6}{9}-\frac{15}{9}\text{i}=-\frac{2}{3}-\frac{5}{3}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
